source.article: External dialogue: crewAI GuardrailProvider conformance governance

workflow.action: admit test vectors, define expected verdicts, recompute results, and use the suite as a GuardrailProvider conformance bar
workflow.trigger: a provider-neutral GuardrailProvider contract needs a credible pass/fail conformance process
workflow.currentState: fixture bytes and verdicts are independently recomputable, but one maintainer currently controls vector admission and expected semantics
workflow.expectedTransition: move normative vector admission to an independently governed home with explicit multi-party admission and ratification rules

failure.scenario: A conformance suite can be mechanically reproducible while remaining normatively centralized because one party chooses the vectors and expected outcomes.
failure.cause: Computational independence and normative independence are treated as if they were the same trust property.
failure.recovery: Separate recomputability from ratifiability; keep vendor-owned suites explicitly labeled until a multi-party admission rule exists.
failure.impact: A provider or ecosystem may overstate neutrality and treat a vendor-owned test set as an authoritative conformance bar without independent governance of the normative cases.

currentSolution.workaround: Publish committed fixture bytes and an independently runnable checker so strangers can recompute and challenge expected verdicts.
currentSolution.limitation: Independent recomputation closes the mechanical review gap but does not determine who is allowed to define the normative test set.

trustRequirement.desiredState: A conformance suite whose computation is independently reproducible and whose normative vector set is governed by an explicit process no single vendor controls.
trustRequirement.invariant: A suite MUST NOT claim neutrality solely because verdicts are independently recomputable; vector admission and ratification must also be externally governed or explicitly identified as vendor-owned.
trustRequirement.verification: Verify both properties separately: (1) unrelated graders derive the same result from published bytes; (2) vector admission and expected-outcome changes follow a documented multi-party rule.
trustRequirement.evidence: Public fixture bytes, independent grader results, admission-policy history, ratification records, and signatures/approvals from more than one governance participant.

productDiscovery.missingCapability: A neutral, multi-party ratification layer for agent-governance conformance vectors, separate from the mechanical checker implementation.
productDiscovery.hypothesis: Conformance infrastructure needs two independent trust axes — computational independence and normative independence — and tools should report them separately.

conversation.nextQuestion: What is the smallest admissibility and multi-signature ratification rule that would let a vendor-owned fixture set become a credible ecosystem conformance bar without creating a new central authority?
